**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 17(b), Term and Termination**

- **Vendor side is fine:** Garman has no termination-for-convenience right; its only exit is Section 17(c) (insolvency events or uncured material default), which is mutual and cause-based.
- **Customer side falls short of preferred:** our convenience right requires 90 days' notice (fallback-level only), and there is no refund of prepaid fees. Given the perpetual licence with annually prepaid maintenance fees (Sections 10 and 17(a)), a mid-year exit would forfeit prepaid amounts — an effective early-termination penalty.
- **Redline (validated, preferred level):** 30 days' notice, exit "without penalty or early-termination charge," and Garman refunds prepaid fees (including maintenance) for the post-termination period; the cease-use/certification mechanics track the shortened notice period. Comment offers 60 days as fallback provided the pro-rata refund survives.
